title: How Long Do Leftovers Last in the Fridge—and When Should You Throw Them Out?

seo.title: How Long Do Leftovers Last in the Fridge?
seo.meta_description: Most cooked leftovers keep 3–4 days at 40°F or below under USDA guidance. Learn cooling rules, exceptions, reheating and when to discard food.
seo.search_intent: General food-safety guidance for refrigerated leftovers.

excerpt: USDA guidance gives most cooked leftovers about 3–4 days in a refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below. That window only applies when food was refrigerated within two hours and kept consistently cold.
content_html:
For many cooked leftovers, the USDA rule is easy to remember: refrigerate within two hours and eat within three to four days. But it is a starting point, not permission to save food that sat warm all afternoon.

The basic U.S. rule

Keep the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below. Refrigerate perishable food within two hours, or one hour when ambient temperature is above 90°F (32°C).

Common refrigerator windows

FoodTypical USDA/FoodSafety.gov range
Cooked meat or poultry leftovers3–4 days
Soups and stews3–4 days
Cooked pizza3–4 days
Hard-cooked eggs1 week
Cooked fish/shellfish leftoversgenerally 3–4 days

Some authorities issue more specific advice for individual foods. Rice is a good example: UK guidance is more conservative because of Bacillus cereus. A universal number should never erase a food-specific rule.

Cooling a large batch

Divide big pots into shallow containers so the center cools quickly. Leaving a deep pot on the counter for hours is not safer than putting food in the refrigerator.

Smell is not a safety test

Mold, slime, fermentation or off odors are obvious discard signals. But pathogens can grow without sensory changes, so a normal smell cannot extend the 3–4 day window.

Does reheating reset the clock?

No. Reheating day-three leftovers does not create another fresh four-day period. Reheat only the portion you need when practical, and heat leftovers to 165°F (74°C).

Freeze before you run out of time

If plans change, freeze leftovers while their storage history is still good. Freezing stops microbial growth but does not undo unsafe room-temperature exposure.

When to discard immediately

  • Food sat out more than two hours, or one hour in high heat.
  • You cannot remember when it was cooked.
  • The refrigerator was too warm for an extended period.
  • There is visible mold or obvious spoilage.
  • It is beyond the recommended refrigerator window.

Frequently asked questions

Are leftovers safe after five days?

Five days is beyond the USDA 3–4 day range for most cooked leftovers.

Can I rely on smell?

No. Smell detects some spoilage but not all foodborne pathogens.

Should I freeze leftovers on day one?

If you know you will not eat them within a few days, early freezing preserves both safety margin and quality.

faq.question: How long do most leftovers last in the fridge?
faq.answer: USDA guidance is generally 3–4 days at 40°F (4°C) or below for many cooked leftovers.

faq.question: Does reheating restart the refrigerator clock?
faq.answer: No. Reheating does not create a new 3–4 day storage period.

faq.question: Can leftovers be safe if they smell normal?
faq.answer: A normal smell does not prove safety; time and temperature history still control the decision.
